title: Book One · Chapter 64: A Place to Put the Note
story:
Mr Han is at home on Sunday morning.

He opens the door. He has a small brush in his hand. Behind him, Bo holds the red bicycle still. A wet patch shines on its back wheel.

Ronan looks away from the bicycle. He gives Mr Han Mum's folded note.

“Mrs Gao has her envelope,” he says. “Mum wrote the full address here.”

Mr Han reads the note. Then he asks Ronan and Mum to come inside.

Bo moves the bicycle to make room. It has a different mark on one handle now. A piece of black cloth is tied there.

“What is that for?” Ronan asks.

“I can find my bike at school,” Bo says. “I look for this black cloth.”

Ronan knows the bicycle without any black cloth. He almost says so. Instead he touches the wooden chair beside him.

Mr Han brings out the address he first wrote down. He puts it beside Mum's note.

“I knew the house,” he says. “I needed to add East Court to the address. I left those two words out. I sent the man while I was busy.”

“The old way of writing it was not clear,” Mum says.

“Yes. And I passed it on.”

Ronan watches Mr Han draw a line through the short address. Beneath it, he writes a longer one.

“Will you tell the man?” Ronan asks.

“I will. He asked about it yesterday. He was worried.”

Bo sits beside Ronan. He holds out the brush.

“Do you want a turn?”

Ronan looks at Mum.

“You may help if you want to,” she says.

They take the bicycle into the little yard. Bo tips water from a cup onto the dirty wheel. Ronan brushes the place near the mudguard. He cleaned this wheel with Dad before. He remembers that day. For a moment, he feels happy. Then he looks at Bo. The bicycle belongs to Bo now.

“You missed there,” Bo says.

“I can see it.”

He says it too sharply. Bo takes the brush from him.

“You can stop now. I can do it.”

Ronan steps away. A drop of muddy water runs over his shoe.

“I used to know every part,” he says.

Bo looks at the red frame. “I know. Dad told me.”

“I did not say you cannot have it.”

“I did not say you did.”

For a moment both boys are quiet. Then Bo points at the black cloth.

“You can know it, and it can be mine.”

Ronan does not have a quick answer.

From the doorway, Mr Han calls, “Come along now. We are ready.” Bo puts the brush down.

Ronan looks once more at the wheel. There is a small line of mud below the place he cleaned.

“There,” he says, more softly.

Bo bends down. “Yes. Thank you.”

Mr Han folds Mum's note and puts it in a drawer beside the corrected address. “Why do you keep both notes?” Ronan asks.

“The new one has the right address,” Mr Han says. “The old address has words missing. I can see those missing words in the new one.”

Bo goes back to the wheel. This time he brings a clean cup of water.

On the way home, Mum walks quietly beside him.

He walks beside her until they reach the tea shop.

“Bo puts cloth on everything,” he says.

“Does he?”

“Perhaps he will tie some to his father.”

Mum laughs. Ronan laughs too. He still feels sad about the bicycle. But he can laugh with Mum too.

At home, he puts Mr Han's reply beside the map. Mum will give it to Mrs Lan after lunch.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- passed it on＝把它转交了
- mudguard＝挡泥板
- sharply＝语气冲
- a turn＝一次轮流机会

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：frame＝车架；muddy＝有泥的。

## 读句提示

**He gives Mr Han Mum's folded note.**

他／把妈妈折好的纸条／交给Mr Han。He指Ronan。

## 理解问题

1. MrHan承认自己漏做了什么？
2. Ronan帮Bo洗车时为什么会有复杂的感受？
